A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rainbow framework. All 47 pages, including appendices A–E, are readable and support comparison. Rendered pages are identical except for pages 1, 4 and 5.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, MRI counterfactuals, downstream evaluations and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix E, including quantitative results in Tables 1, 3 and 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix E, including natural-image, brain-MRI and chest-X-ray evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Appendix C retain the same graph sampling, graph decoder, condition blending, diffusion inference and training losses. Figure 1's graphical edits do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Flickr30k/COCO natural-image coverage, pooled brain-MRI datasets and CheXpert data. Generation, editing, counterfactual and downstream age-prediction tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 3 includes SD3.5, SD2-1, CADS, PAG and DDIM; Table 1 includes GAN and LDM; Table 4 includes RadEdit and SD1.5. Qualitative comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same evaluation metrics, model configurations, sample counts and training budgets, including the natural-image evaluation using 60 prompts and 40 images per prompt.

E4.justification: The trajectory-count, node-count and sparsity ablations, guidance-scale comparisons, latent-edge manipulations, failure examples and MRI fidelity analyses are unchanged in the main text and Appendix E.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical across the quantitative tables, plots and checklist responses. Neither version adds or revises run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimation or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: All quantitative and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Rainbow retains IS 10.45 and Inception VS 28.90 in Table 3, and FID 1.27 and VS 7.16 in Table 4. Appendix result figures also render identically.

T1.justification: The GFlowNet formulation, losses and mathematical material in Appendix C are unchanged. Equations 3–6 shift slightly on page 5 but retain the same mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about capturing condition uncertainty, compatibility with pretrained conditional generators, and improved diversity, fidelity and downstream performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Appendix B's limitations are identical, including computational cost, latent-graph interpretability and the need for anatomical plausibility checks before clinical use.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1, Table 2 and Appendix D retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training times. Data/code availability statements and resource links are unchanged apart from the paper's own version permalink.

R1.justification: Section 5, the references and novelty positioning are unchanged. No cited works or substantive relationships to previous research are added or removed.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 25 October 2025 to v2 dated 18 December 2025. Body wording, headings, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives cosmetic edits, notably changing the lower graph-decoder embedding/RNN/pooling illustration from pink/red to green and adjusting diagram spacing and arrows. Pages 4–5 undergo slight reflow; all other figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 updates the version stamp and makes small cosmetic changes to Figure 1 and nearby layout. The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain identical, with no clear correction of a substantive readability problem or meaningful overall quality difference.
